name: ProteinMPNN
one_liner: Message-passing graph neural network for inverse protein folding whose designed sequences are ranked by the model log probability, with AlphaFold2 structure prediction and wet-lab crystallization used to measure whether they fold.

loop.proposes: An SE(3)-invariant message-passing neural network decodes amino-acid sequences conditioned on a target 3D protein backbone.
loop.judged_by: The model log probability ranks designed sequences; AlphaFold2 / ESMFold single-sequence structure prediction (pLDDT and backbone RMSD) plus wet-lab SEC, cryo-EM, and X-ray crystallography measure whether they refold.
loop.steers: Tied-position symmetry constraints shape decoding, and designed sequences are ranked by the model log probability.

headline_result: Achieved 52.4% native sequence recovery (vs. 32.9% for Rosetta) and rescued previously failed de novo protein cyclic oligomers, nanoparticles, and binders in wet-lab crystallography.
caveat: Assumes a designable target backbone; cannot fix a backbone with severe steric clashes on its own.
beyond_harness_note: A message-passing 3D graph network proposes sequences that are ranked by the model log probability; AlphaFold refolding RMSD and X-ray crystallography measure whether they fold.
algorithmic_authority: The model log probability for ranking; AlphaFold2 refolding and X-ray crystallography / cryo-EM as measures of whether designs fold

sources.title: Robust deep learning-based protein sequence design using ProteinMPNN (Science, 2022)

verification.notes: Checked against Dauparas et al., Science 378(6615), 2022.
